cards.headline: A warning label on an aerosol can started the song
cards.snippet: British indie band Alt-J's "Breezeblocks" began with a warning label. Singer Joe Newman read an aerosol can that said it "may contain traces... of something that may be flammable." He turned that into the lyric "she may contain the urge to run away," which became part of the song's refrain. Newman has described the song, from the band's 2012 debut album An Awesome Wave, as being about wanting someone so much that you want to hurt yourself and them.
cards.context: Newman's account of how the song began.

cards.headline: The ending is borrowed from Where the Wild Things Are
cards.snippet: Alt-J's "Breezeblocks" (2012) ends with the refrain "Please don't go, I'll eat you whole / I love you so," which adapts a line from Maurice Sendak's 1963 children's book Where the Wild Things Are. Sendak wrote, "Oh, please don't go – we'll eat you up – we love you so!" Singer Joe Newman has said the book partly inspired the song and the rest of the band's debut album, An Awesome Wave.
cards.context: Sendak's line from the 1963 book, which the lyric adapts.

cards.headline: The song's real chorus, according to everyone
cards.snippet:
99% “please don’t go I love you so
1% “breezeblocks”
cards.context: Most listeners remember the "please don't go" outro far more than the title.
